description: Library staff are preparing a public program and need to align room setup, assistive devices, large-print materials, interpretation support, and participant-specific accessibility requests.

user_profile.persona: 37-year-old public programs librarian coordinating an inclusive event
user_profile.context: The event itself is planned, but accessibility details are currently spread across RSVP notes and staff memory
user_profile.communication_style: Inclusive and detail-oriented, wants accommodations treated as core logistics rather than add-ons

fact_sheet.fact: The public program is titled 'Modern Calligraphy Workshop'.
The workshop is scheduled for Saturday, October 26, 2024, from 2:00 PM to 4:00 PM.
The event will be held in Community Room B at the Oakridge Public Library.
Lena Petrova is the lead Public Programs Librarian coordinating the event.
The room setup request specifies five round tables, each seating a maximum of six participants.
A minimum pathway width of 48 inches must be maintained between all tables to ensure wheelchair accessibility.
The presenter's lectern must be an adjustable height model, set to 40 inches at the start of the event.
Overhead lighting in Community Room B will be set to 800 lux to accommodate participants with low vision.
Participant RSVP #1152, Anika Sharma, requested a seat with a clear line of sight to the ASL interpreter.
Participant RSVP #1201, David Chen, requested a workspace with an additional task light and access to a power outlet for a personal device.
Participant RSVP #1099, Maria Flores, has a severe latex allergy; all provided art supplies have been confirmed to be latex-free.
Two participants, identified in RSVP notes #1088 and #1124, have requested left-handed calligraphy pens.
An FM assistive listening system has been requested by participant RSVP #1138.
The library is renting one Phonak Roger FM system from AccessTech Solutions under purchase order #78-AC9.
The rented FM system is scheduled for delivery to the library's receiving dock on Friday, October 25, 2024, by 3:00 PM.
The library will provide a portable video magnifier (CCTV), model Ruby XL HD, for participant David Chen (RSVP #1201).
Ten copies of the workshop instruction booklet have been printed in large-print format using 18-point Arial font.
The large-print booklets are stored in the Programs Office, in Cabinet 4, labeled 'Calligraphy Workshop - LP'.
A screen-reader accessible PDF of the instruction booklet was emailed to all 28 registered participants on October 22, 2024.
An American Sign Language (ASL) interpreter is required for the full two-hour duration of the workshop.
The library has contracted with LinguaConnect Services to provide the ASL interpreter.
The assigned interpreter's name is Elias Vance, and his confirmation number is LC-8842.
Elias Vance is scheduled to arrive at the library's welcome desk at 1:30 PM for setup and briefing.
A specific armless chair and a dedicated floor lamp have been placed at the front-right of the room for the interpreter.
The total cost for the interpretation service for this event is $350, invoiced under #INV-2024-512.
Marco Diaz, the Facilities Coordinator, is responsible for executing the physical room setup based on diagram v3.1.
All accommodation details are centralized in a shared document titled 'Calligraphy_Accessibility_Plan' on the library's G-Drive.
Lena Petrova and Marco Diaz will conduct a final accessibility and setup walkthrough of Community Room B at 1:00 PM on the day of the event.
A reserved parking space, #A-04, located closest to the main entrance, has been designated for the ASL interpreter.
Power strips will be provided at Table 1 and Table 4 to accommodate participants' electronic devices.
A printed seating chart is attached to the event coordination binder, placing Anika Sharma and David Chen at Table 1.
The workshop has a total of 28 registered participants out of a possible 30.
The library's portable video magnifier is stored in the Assistive Tech closet, key #112, held at the main circulation desk.
